title: Where your phone comes from
hook: Follow a smartphone from the mine to your pocket.
notes: An illustrative, typical smartphone supply chain. Specific suppliers and shares vary by brand and model and change every year.

scenes.title: Dug out of the ground
scenes.text: Cobalt from the DR Congo. Lithium from Australia and Chile. Rare earths from China. Tin from Indonesia. A phone contains dozens of elements.

scenes.title: Refined in China
scenes.text: Much of it travels to China, which refines most of the world's cobalt, lithium and rare earths.

scenes.title: Chips: a global relay
scenes.text: Designed in California. Made in Taiwan, on machines that only one Dutch company, ASML, can build. Memory from South Korea, camera sensors from Japan.

scenes.title: Assembly
scenes.text: Final assembly mostly happens in China, with a fast-growing share in India and Vietnam.

scenes.title: To your pocket
scenes.text: By the time a phone reaches a shop in Vienna, its parts may have travelled further than a trip around the Earth.
